scope: One model family with provider-disclosed cutoffs, used to vary cutoff at fixed size and size at fixed cutoff.
why: Elsewhere in this paper parameter count is confounded with family, recipe and cutoff. These two arms compare models within one family while holding size or the reported cutoff fixed.
cutoffs_are_provider_claims: Cutoff dates are taken from Meta's model cards. They are claims by the provider, not measurements; our own attempt to estimate an effective cutoff from accuracy curves failed (see the estimator negative result).

arm_a_cutoff_varies_size_fixed.controls_reading: The before-both and after-both date groups provide comparison contrasts for the between-cutoff group. Provider cutoff dates do not establish which answers either model knows. Training differences remain confounded with release dates.
arm_a_cutoff_varies_size_fixed.reading: Same size and family, with different provider-reported cutoffs. The contrasts do not isolate a causal cutoff effect.

arm_b_size_varies_cutoff_fixed.primary_is_precision_matched: The primary slope uses only the bfloat16 rungs. Adding a 4-bit rung would put a precision difference back into the one analysis built to remove nuisance variables, so the quantised extension is reported separately rather than pooled.

slope_bootstrap.note: quiz-clustered bootstrap, conditional on these rungs; the primary inference for this arm because the exact permutation test is resolution-limited at this few rungs
quiz-clustered bootstrap, conditional on these rungs; the primary inference for this arm because the exact permutation test is resolution-limited at this few rungs

extension_all_rungs_mixed_precision.caveat: includes a 4-bit rung; the parameter range widens to 70x but precision is no longer held fixed

slope.note: quiz-clustered bootstrap, conditional on these rungs; the primary inference for this arm because the exact permutation test is resolution-limited at this few rungs

vs_main_ladder.reading: Fraction of the shared-boundary slope that survives holding the cutoff fixed. Well below 1 supports this paper's argument that a shared calendar boundary measures cutoff offset as well as scale; near 1 would mean the confound was not doing the work.

arm_b_size_varies_cutoff_fixed.caveat: Llama-3.2 1B/3B are distilled from larger Llama-3.1 models rather than independently pretrained, so this arm holds cutoff and family fixed but not training procedure. 4 rungs; the exact permutation test is reported but is resolution-limited at this few rungs, so the quiz bootstrap is the primary inference.

arm_c_same_release_only_size_differs.reading: Two models of one release, same data and recipe, same disclosed cutoff, same quantization; only parameter count differs. This is a two-point contrast, so it carries no slope uncertainty of its own -- each gap's interval is reported and the implied slope is descriptive.

verdict.reading: Arm A holds size fixed and Arm B holds the reported cutoff fixed. Training differences remain. The three-rung Arm B bootstrap is conditional on this roster and is driven by the 8B point. Its exhaustive size-label permutation p is 4/6, with floor 1/6.
